newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen's new govt vows to pursue economic reforms.
newsitem.headline: Yemen's new govt vows to pursue economic reforms.

text.p: Yemen's new government promised on Thursday to continue sensitive economic reforms launched in 1995 to liberalise the market and trim soaring budget and balance of payments deficits.

"We will continue economic and administrative reforms to rectify the overall economic situation," Prime Minister Faraj Said Bin Ghanem said in a speech outlining his government's programme to the newly-elected parliament.
"The Yemeni economy is still passing through a critical stage and this dictates the necessity to continue implementing a string of measures in monetary, credit and financial areas."

President Ali Abdullah Saleh last month appointed Bin Ghanem, a Polish-educated independent economist from southern Yemen, to head a new government after the April 27 elections, the first since a 1994 civil war nearly tore the country apart.
The 301-member chamber, in which Saleh's ruling party holds the majority, will debate the government's programme before putting it to a vote of confidence in the next weeks.
The impoverished Arab state began economic reforms three years ago in agreement with the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
Officials say the programme has shown some positive signs, helping cut unemployment and inflation and boosting foreign currency reserves.
